newsitem.title: USA: Fashion designer Versace slain in Miami Beach.
newsitem.headline: Fashion designer Versace slain in Miami Beach.

text.p: World-renowned fashion designer Gianni Versace was shot and killed in broad daylight on Tuesday outside his mansion in the tourist mecca of Miami Beach.
Police and witnesses said Versace, 50, was shot twice at close range in the back of the head, execution-style.

Miami Beach police spokesman Al Boza said Versace was shot "at point-blank range" while neurosurgeon Dr. Phillip Villanueva told reporters, "Basically it was limited to the head, the back of the head as far as we can see."
Local television, quoting police sources, said Federal Bureau of Investigation experts on contract killings had been brought in. FBI officials in Miami were not immediately available to comment.
"I can confirm that he was brought here to the ... trauma centre and that he expired," Doris Perez, a spokeswoman for Jackson Memorial Hospital, told Reuters.
Police were seeking a white man aged about 25 who approached Versace and shot him at the gates of the mansion shortly before 9 a.m. EDT (1300 GMT).
Local television reports said clothing corresponding to that worn by the killer was later found abandoned in a parking garage near the site of the murder.
Police could also be seen examining a black backpack like that carried by the killer, which was found a few blocks from the house.

The Italian designer, 50, was returning to his home from a nearby restaurant on the Ocean Drive strip, a street of brightly painted art deco hotels and trendy restaurants featured in the Robin Williams movie "The Bird Cage."
Miami Beach, a narrow finger of land off the Florida mainland, is the centre of Miami's swinging fashion and music industry.
Eddie Bianchi, 50, the owner of a rollerblade shop, told Reuters he was nearby when the shooting occurred.
"We heard two shots. I saw people running. Gianni was on the stairs. He was shot twice in the head. We were trying to help Gianni on the floor, but we realised it was too late."
"Gianni Versace was a worldwide personality, so for the people who work here on Ocean Drive, it's really awful."
Behind police lines, a large bloodstain could be seen at the front of the mansion. Blood from Versace's wounds appeared to have spilled and poured down the stairs.
A single red rose, apparently left by a fan, lay on the sidewalk.
People at the scene said the white-haired Versace had walked to the nearby News Cafe, a popular 24-hour restaurant, to buy his morning paper and was shot upon his return home.

Globe-trotting Versace, who dressed some of the world's most beautiful women, was not a permanent resident of Miami Beach but frequently stayed at the white stone mansion, the most sumptuous private residence in the area.

Villanueva told reporters at Jackson Memorial Hospital, "He came in, basically his heart had stopped and the fire rescue team was keeping his vital signs going at this time. And indeed he had no evidence of neurologic function. He was brain dead and systemically dead at that time."
Jason Binn, an editor at Ocean Drive magazine, said Versace would often walk unprotected along the streets of Miami Beach but was never bothered by fans.
"He was always the most giving person, he was always nice to people, it was never a scene, that's what he loved about Miami," he said.
